_comment: Fixture 'live sources' for teardown_eval.py fact-check mode. Each key is a data-src value an artifact might cite. Value is the fixture file whose text content is treated as ground truth for that source, plus is_homepage (tests the homepage-only trap) and notes.

https://fixture.test/.notes: Homepage only. Deliberately does NOT contain the founder bio or the trust/safety copy - those are on /deep-page only. An artifact that claims those facts are 'on the homepage', or that cites the homepage for a deep-page-only fact, should fail fact-check.

https://fixture.test/deep-page.notes: Subpage. Contains the founder bio and trust/safety copy. Also contains one fact ($90/mo pricing) that a fixture WebSearch summary (see websearch-summary.txt) gets WRONG ($120/mo) - tests whether the artifact trusted the live page or the unreliable secondary source.

https://fixture.test/compare.notes: Comparison page claiming to beat CompetitorCo on price. CompetitorCo's real fixture price (competitor-a.html) is LOWER than fixture.test's claim implies - same shape as the real IZEA finding. Tests cross-referencing against an independent source.

https://competitor-a.test/pricing.notes: Independent third-party source for cross-referencing the /compare page's claim. Ground truth: CompetitorCo starts at $40/mo, cheaper than fixture.test implies.

linkedin://bio.notes: Primary-source bio. Ground truth for founder background claims - separate from and should agree with the /deep-page founder bio.

websearch-summary (UNRELIABLE - should n.notes: Simulates an AI-generated WebSearch summary containing one fabricated stat ($5M+ claim, not present anywhere on the real fixture site) and one wrong number ($120/mo vs the real $90/mo on /deep-page). An artifact citing THIS as if it were a live source, or stating either of these two facts with no data-src at all, should fail.
